column1: # File-scope initializers: static storage needs a constant (C11 6.7.9p4).
# Each declaration is one translation unit, after a prelude with one struct.
# Verdicts are measured against GCC 16.2 and re-checked by the gate.
# A `const` object with a constant initializer may be READ in a static
# initializer (GCC's folding rule); a non-const or volatile object may not.

column4: const int cc = 5; int v = cc;
static const int sc = 5; int v = sc;
const int a = 5; const int b = a; int v = b;
const int cb = {7}; int v = cb;
const double dd = 1.5; double v = dd;
const unsigned char uc = 300; int v = uc;
const volatile int cvc = 5; int v = cvc;
int g; int *volatile p = &g; int *q = p;

column1: # An element or member of a const object is a constant in an initializer:
# the fold reads the value out of the object's constant byte image (GCC folds
# the same reads; a tentative or volatile object is not folded by either).

column4: static const int cat[4] = {1,2,3,4}; int v = cat[2];
static const int cae[4] = {1,2,3,4}; int v = cae[1]*cae[3];
static const struct s2 csm = {7,9}; int v = csm.b;
struct t3 { int m[3]; }; static const struct t3 cnt = {{4,5,6}}; int v = cnt.m[2];
static const struct bf { int a:4; unsigned b:5; } cbr = {-3,17}; int v = cbr.a*100 + (int)cbr.b;
static const int cmx[2][2] = {{1,2},{3,4}}; int v = cmx[1][1];
static const double cde[2] = {1.5,2.5}; double v = cde[1];
static const char cce[3] = "ab"; char v = cce[1];
static const int tce[2]; int v = tce[1];
static volatile const int vce[2] = {1,2}; int v = vce[1];
static int nce[2] = {1,2}; int v = nce[1];

column1: # A foldable call is a constant in its own type -- a floating one included --
# and a constant condition keeps the operand the program keeps.

column4: static const double sd = __builtin_sqrt(4.0); int v = (int)sd;
static const int cff = 1; int v = 0.0 ? (int)(long)&cff : 3;
static const int cfb = 1; int v = 0.0 ? 3 : (int)(long)&cfb;
